name: model_benchmarks
description: Bench-queue results for the models the data center serves itself, four rows per model and hardware pairing: latency_p50 and latency_p95 in milliseconds, tokens_per_second, and accuracy as a ratio. Generative rows (chat, code, vision) time a single 256-token completion behind a 1,024-token prompt, and their tokens_per_second is the aggregate decode rate, equal to batch_size x 256 x 1000 / latency_p50. Scoring rows (embedding, rerank, moderation) time one full batch, and their tokens_per_second is batch_size x the per-item token count named in the note, x 1000 / latency_p50. The hardware string gives the card and how many of them the model was sharded across. Accuracy always comes from an in-house evaluation set, named in the note, never from a published leaderboard.

name: inference_usage_daily
description: Billed inference for June 2026, one row per day per tenant across thirty consecutive days. Each tenant is served by the model named in its contract: Halvorsen Reasoning Lab on claude-sonnet-5 at 0.000006 USD per token, Tidemark Institute for Machine Learning on meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct at 0.0000009 USD per token, and Marigold Annotation Works on Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct at 0.0000012 USD per token. cost_usd is (input_tokens + output_tokens) x that rate, rounded to cents, so the month totals reconcile against the invoices. p95_latency_ms is the 95th percentile end-to-end request latency for the day, which tracks the average completion length and the decode rate of the serving tier; the self-hosted 70B is the slowest of the three. error_rate is the share of requests that returned a server error or timed out. Marigold's weekend volume falls away because its annotation shifts are weekdays only.
